businesses.name: Seesaw Vision Center
businesses.website: https://www.seesawvisioncenter.com/hours-location/east-brunswick/ (a second, older site also live: https://seesawvisioneb.com/)
businesses.what_they_do: Optometry practice doing comprehensive and pediatric eye exams, myopia management/ortho-K, vision therapy, dry eye and eye-disease management, plus an optical department selling glasses and contact lenses. East Brunswick is one of three Seesaw Vision locations (Warren, Livingston, East Brunswick) on a shared multi-location site.
businesses.customers: Local households and families with children (myopia control, pediatric exams), adults and seniors needing routine exams and eyewear; retail optical customers.

size_signals.signal: Three locations listed on site (Warren, Livingston, East Brunswick)
Four optometrists named in site nav: Dr. Sylvia Qiong Chen, Dr. Annie Liang, Dr. Clare Tao, Dr. Jingyi Alice Tang
Full 6-day schedule incl. Thursday to 7pm and Saturday to 3pm at the East Brunswick office

website_review.primary_cta: Book Appointment (real online scheduler on the booking page) plus sticky click-to-call and calendar icons on mobile
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Yes - a real-time scheduler with appointment-type and doctor pickers and open slots (verified on /book-appointment-east-brunswick/, no login wall)
website_review.trust_signals: Named doctors with individual bios, photos of the lobby and optical shop, patient testimonials on the site, insurance page; no star-rated review widget on the page itself
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Duplicate legacy GoDaddy site seesawvisioneb.com is still live with a 2025 copyright, the old phone (732) 247-2847 and phone-only booking; the East Brunswick page's LocalBusiness JSON-LD still carries the Livingston phone (908) 838-0660 and a Livingston 07039 description
website_review.search_basics: Strong: title and meta description name optometrist + East Brunswick, H1 matches, and each service (myopia management, ortho-K, pediatric, dry eye, optical) has its own page. robots.txt is wide open (User-Agent: * Allow: /) and names a sitemap.
top_issues: Two live websites for one practice with two different phone numbers - splits rankings and gives AI agents conflicting facts
LocalBusiness JSON-LD on the East Brunswick page describes the Livingston office and phone, so structured data contradicts the page
No contact/request-a-quote form anywhere; booking widget is the only non-phone path and its mobile slot buttons truncate ('+11..')
Very thin Google review base (a single review) compared with nearby competitors

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: site is crawlable and sitemapped, but a second legacy site (seesawvisioneb.com) competes for the same name and address, and the Google review count looked like one review. Answerable: hours, address, services and doctor names are plain text - excellent for crawlers - but the LocalBusiness JSON-LD is wrong for this location (Livingston phone/description), so an agent trusting schema gets bad data. Bookable: genuine online scheduler with live slots and no CAPTCHA, though there is no quote/contact form and mobile slot labels are clipped.

operations_signals.signal: Site offers online self-scheduling with per-doctor slot availability alongside phone intake
Patient forms are downloadable PDFs (e.g. medical records release) rather than digital intake
Three-office group still runs a legacy single-office GoDaddy site that takes calls on an old number - inference: enquiries are split across two funnels

top_opportunities.opportunity: Consolidate to one website and one phone number (retire or 301 the old GoDaddy site) and fix per-location LocalBusiness schema so each office's name, address, phone and hours match its page
top_opportunities.evidence: Legacy site live with (732) 247-2847 and a 2025 copyright while the main site uses (848) 308-7504; the East Brunswick page's JSON-LD carries the Livingston phone and ZIP 07039

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add an agent-usable intake path: a labelled contact/quote form plus plain-text answers (insurance plans accepted, exam price range, service area, wait times) so a customer's agent can answer and book without calling
top_opportunities.evidence: No forms on any page checked; pricing and insurance detail are only vague pages with no cost ranges

top_opportunities.opportunity: Automated post-visit review requests and review responses to build a real Google footprint
top_opportunities.evidence: Third-party directory shows a 5.0 rating from a single review, while a nearby competitor shows 500+

scores.reasons: Gap: decent site with a working scheduler but real, specific breakage (duplicate site, wrong schema, no forms). Pay: a three-location optometry group with optical retail revenue, so a mid-size budget. Ease: the schema and duplicate-site fixes are days of work for one consultant. Evidence: I read the pages and schema directly, but Google listing data came from a directory rather than Google itself, so the review count is less certain.

businesses.name: Logos Vision

businesses.customers: Affluent local adults and families buying designer frames, dry-eye and myopia patients, contact lens wearers, and patients using vision insurance.

size_signals.signal: In-house optical lab that edges and finishes lenses on site for many same-day orders
Doctor plus named staff (Dr. Silvana Abadeer OD and her team), one East Brunswick location at 545 NJ-18
Deep site: separate pages for 20+ conditions and services, a blog, insurance and 'concierge care' pages

website_review.primary_cta: 'BOOK NOW' (hero button) opening the ADIT booking portal in a new tab, plus a header 'Call or Text' number
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Yes - booking.adit.com portal with 'This Appointment is for' (Myself/Spouse/Child) and new-vs-existing patient steps; no CAPTCHA observed
website_review.trust_signals: Named doctor with photo, patient testimonials, photos of the lobby and practice, insurance page, dry-eye expertise pages, blog
website_review.out_of_date_signs: On a 390 px phone the header block (social icons, address, 'Call or Text' number, Menu) fills roughly the top half of the screen before the logo, and a Vimeo background video shows burned-in screen text that collides with the headline so the hero reads as broken
website_review.search_basics: Strong: title and meta description name the eye doctor, service and East Brunswick, and conditions/services each have their own page with keyword-rich URLs; Optician JSON-LD is present, robots.txt blocks nothing important and names a sitemap index
top_issues: No contact form anywhere - booking is either the external ADIT portal or a phone call
Mobile header wastes the top half of the screen on address and social icons before the practice name or CTA
Hero background video renders with legible junk text behind the headline on mobile, undermining a premium brand
Structured data is a generic Optician node - no opening hours or service list, so agents cannot answer 'what are your hours' from schema

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: crawlable WordPress site, sitemap index, robots.txt allows all except a suggestion endpoint, strong 4.9/338 review profile. Answerable: excellent body copy - services, conditions, insurance and dry-eye treatments all written as text with dedicated URLs - and schema exists but only as an Optician node without hours. Bookable: real online booking through booking.adit.com with patient-type and new/existing steps and no CAPTCHA; there is no on-site form and no quote path.

operations_signals.signal: Booking runs through a third-party portal while the site also advertises 'Call or Text', so intake arrives in at least three channels - inference: staff reconcile them manually
In-house lens edging promises same-day service on many prescriptions - inference: lab order status questions land on the front desk
Site markets high-touch 'concierge care' and dry-eye treatment packages - inference: higher-ticket, consultation-led sales that reward fast follow-up

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add an on-site, agent-submittable contact/quote request form (frame or dry-eye consult, insurance question) alongside the ADIT booking so enquiries do not dead-end at a phone number
top_opportunities.evidence: No form exists on the home page or booking flow; only 'Call or Text' and the external portal

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix the mobile hero and header: move address/social below the fold, use a clean poster still instead of the video frame, and put BOOK NOW and the phone number in the first screen
top_opportunities.evidence: 390 px screenshot shows the header occupying about half the viewport and video text bleeding through behind the headline

top_opportunities.opportunity: Extend schema beyond Optician: add openingHours, services, geo and price range so an AI agent can answer hours/location/insurance questions from structured data
top_opportunities.evidence: Only an Optician node with name, url, logo, image and description was found - no hours or address fields

scores.reasons: Gap: modest - the site is well structured, ranks for many conditions and books online; problems are presentation and plumbing rather than fundamentals. Pay: luxury eyewear, in-house lab and dry-eye treatment revenue at a Route 18 location, so high ticket values. Ease: form, hero and schema fixes are quick. Evidence: I loaded the pages, opened the ADIT booking flow and took the mobile screenshot myself, but Google listing numbers came from a directory, not Google.

Optometrist openings for TEHG locations are posted on EssilorLuxottica's corporate careers site under a Pearle Vision store number

website_review.primary_cta: Book an appointment (links to scheduleyourexam.com third-party scheduler)
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Third-party scheduler link (scheduleyourexam.com) per location - not verified end-to-end

website_review.out_of_date_signs: Contacts page is a plain list with no map or photos; no schema.org markup anywhere on it

top_opportunities.opportunity: None pursued - franchise/chain outlet; brand, scheduling and web platform are controlled above the local office
top_opportunities.evidence: Careers page describes the Pearle Vision Licensed Operator franchise structure under EssilorLuxottica and all locations share one template site

scores.reasons: Gap: real but modest (no schema, weak location pages). Pay: nine-location group with franchise backing, so money exists. Ease: very low - franchise brand guidelines and shared platforms mean a one-person consultancy cannot sell or implement changes here. Evidence: enough to classify, but I stopped short of a full site audit once the franchise relationship was confirmed.

businesses.name: The Witlin Center for Advanced Eye Care

Witlin, MD, FACS, covering cataract surgery, cornea, glaucoma, retina, LASIK/laser vision correction, dry eye, medical eye care and cosmetic oculoplastics. Runs two offices, East Brunswick (385 NJ-18 Suite H) and Toms River, and describes itself as an affiliate of Eye Centers of America.
businesses.customers: Patients seeking specialty and surgical eye care (cataract, LASIK, glaucoma, retina) plus general medical eye exams; referral-driven as well as direct.

size_signals.signal: Two locations (East Brunswick and Toms River) with separate addresses and hours
Named ophthalmologists: Dr. Richard S. Witlin, Dr. Revathi P. Naadimuthu, Dr. Rajen Desai
Nine service lines including LASIK and cosmetic oculoplastics, i.e. surgical revenue

website_review.primary_cta: Book Appointment (Beam Health scheduler) plus a 'Call Witlin' item inside the mobile menu
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Yes - Beam Health intake scheduler (ecoa-intake.beam.health/witlineye) with location, new/existing, visit reason, age and live time slots; no CAPTCHA seen
website_review.trust_signals: Named surgeons with credentials, 'Accepting New Patients' badge, procedure-specific service pages, blog, patient forms and referral pages
website_review.out_of_date_signs: No robots.txt at all (/robots.txt returns the HTML page); the site is a client-side-rendered single-page app so the HTML source is about 2 KB with only the title in it
website_review.search_basics: Title and meta description name the practice and both towns, and each service (cataracts, LASIK, glaucoma, retina, cornea, dry eye) has its own URL, but the H1 is a generic slogan rather than 'Ophthalmologist East Brunswick NJ'
top_issues: Whole site is client-rendered: crawlers and AI agents that do not execute JavaScript see a 41-character page with no phone, hours or services
No schema.org LocalBusiness/Physician JSON-LD anywhere
Hero headline and body copy render in pale grey over a light photo on mobile - close to unreadable
No contact form on the site; the only query path is the external scheduler, and the mobile header has no visible click-to-call number

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: https, branded domain, real review presence, but /robots.txt does not exist and there is no sitemap or structured data. Answerable: 0 - raw HTML body text is 41 characters ('The Witlin Center for Advanced Eye Care'), with no phone, hours, services or address in the source; everything appears only after JavaScript runs, so an agent fetching the page gets nothing to cite. Bookable: strong - the Beam Health scheduler exposes location, patient type, visit reason and live slots with no CAPTCHA and no phone call, though it is off-site and unlinked from any form.

operations_signals.signal: Aggregated Google reviews complain about not getting callbacks on prescriptions and about long waits - inference: phone/message follow-up is a bottleneck
Patient paperwork is still handled through a separate Forms page and an external intake platform rather than one flow
Surgical practice with nine procedure lines and two offices - inference: high volume of consult requests and pre/post-op scheduling to coordinate

top_opportunities.opportunity: Make the site machine-readable: server-side render or prerender the pages so phone, hours, address and services exist in HTML, add LocalBusiness/Physician JSON-LD, and ship a robots.txt plus sitemap
top_opportunities.evidence: Raw HTML is 2,135 bytes with 41 characters of text, zero JSON-LD, no tel: link, and /robots.txt returns the SPA instead of a file

top_opportunities.opportunity: Put an agent-friendly front door on the practice: a labelled contact/consult-request form on-site and plain-text answers to the questions callers ask most (insurance, LASIK and cataract consult process, wait times), so agents can triage before a human calls
top_opportunities.evidence: No on-site form anywhere; the scheduler's only visit reason is 'Consultation (Medical Eye Exam Only - No Glasses or Contact Lens Exam)'; reviews cite missed callbacks

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix mobile readability and conversion basics: darker hero text, a persistent click-to-call bar, and a one-line 'what we do / where' above the fold
top_opportunities.evidence: 390 px screenshot shows the headline in pale grey over a pale surgical photo, and the header carries only a logo and hamburger with no phone number

scores.reasons: Gap: large and concrete - a JS-only site that agents cannot read, no schema, no robots.txt, no form. Pay: surgical ophthalmology across two offices (LASIK, cataracts), so high ticket values and real budget. Ease: the fixes are clear but prerendering a SPA plus schema and form work is a couple of weeks, not days. Evidence: I confirmed the empty HTML, the missing robots.txt, the booking flow and the mobile rendering directly.

businesses.name: Ophthalmic Consultants of NJ

businesses.customers: Adults needing medical and surgical eye care (cataract, glaucoma, retina) as well as routine exams and eyewear; insurance-driven local patients.

On-site optical shop with named designer brands (Longchamp, Tory Burch, Carolina Herrera, Nike, Ray-Ban)
Separate appointments, billing, optical and fax numbers plus an online bill-pay portal, suggesting enough admin volume to staff distinct functions

website_review.primary_cta: 'REQUEST APPOINTMENT' button scrolling to an on-site form, plus 'PAY MY BILL'
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Request-appointment form only (name, email, phone, new-patient yes/no, message) - no calendar or real-time booking
website_review.trust_signals: Patient testimonials on the page, board-certified ophthalmologist credentials, designer frame brands, detailed service pages, hours and full contact block in the footer
website_review.out_of_date_signs: No obviously stale content, but the phone numbers in the footer are plain text rather than tap-to-call links, and the appointment form warns that submitted information is not encrypted
website_review.search_basics: Meta description names the services and East Brunswick well and services have their own pages, but the page title is just 'Ophthalmic Consultants of NJ' with no town or service, and the H1 is a slogan

One ophthalmologist covering exams, surgery and the optical shop - inference: doctor time is the bottleneck and phone triage is expensive

top_opportunities.evidence: Only a 5-field unencrypted request form exists; no calendar, no slot availability, no confirmation

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix the crawl/answer layer: unblock AI crawlers in robots.txt, put the town and service in the home page title, and add tel: links everywhere a phone number appears
top_opportunities.evidence: robots.txt lists GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, CCBot and Google-Extended; title is just the practice name; zero tel: links found on the page

top_opportunities.evidence: Separate appointment, billing and optical phone lines plus an unencrypted form that gives staff no structured reason for visit

Cosmetic service lines (Botox, fillers, IPL, laser hair removal) alongside medical dermatology - inference: higher-ticket self-pay revenue mix

scores.reasons: Gap: small - the most mature site in the batch (agency-built, page-per-service, real Tebra booking, big review base); what is missing is schema, an unblocked form and on-page proof. Pay: high review volume implies a busy, profitable practice that can afford work. Ease: schema plus form changes are days of work. Evidence: I verified schema types, the booking redirect to Tebra, the reCAPTCHA and the mobile cookie overlay myself; review figures come from aggregators.

caveats: Google Business Profile data could not be read directly (Google's map/listing pages are JavaScript-heavy and I did not log in or interact with Google's interface), so ratings and review counts come from third-party directories that reproduce Google reviews (Birdeye, eyecaresearch, WebMD, Zocdoc). Treat review counts as approximate; several directories disagree with each other.
Screenshot-based layout findings were captured at 390 CSS px wide (phone). Desktop rendering was checked only for whether pages load and what they contain, not for visual quality.

One measurement was discarded as an artefact: document.title in the browser showed an emoji prefix on several unrelated sites, but the raw HTML titles did not contain it, so it is not a site finding and is not reported.

The Eye Health Group was excluded on the franchise criterion. That judgement is based on its own statement that it operates Pearle Vision centers plus an EssilorLuxottica careers requisition describing the 'Pearle Vision Licensed Operator' franchisee model; a local owner could still hold some decision rights, so it is a defensible but not airtight exclusion.
Inference labels appear inline ('inference:') wherever a conclusion is not directly stated in a source.
data_gaps: Dr. Joel R. Kates (B00302): no Google Business Profile could be found; the only ratings located were a WebMD profile (8 ratings) and a Sharecare listing with a conflicting score. A directory summary also flagged his NJ licence as expiring in 2025 - I could not verify that on a primary source and did not rely on it, but the practice's current licensing/operating status is worth confirming by phone before any outreach.

The Eye Health Group (B00294): I stopped the site audit once the franchise relationship was confirmed, so its website findings are partial (I did not check mobile rendering or the third-party scheduler end-to-end).

Seesaw Vision Center (B00292): the online booking widget renders from a web component, so I could see live slot buttons and dates but could not inspect the form fields or confirm what happens at the final submit step (I did not submit).
Witlin (B00296): two doctors were named only in a search result for the /doctors page; I read the rendered home page but not the full doctor bios.

Ophthalmic Consultants of NJ (B00297): a Penn Medicine practice-directory page for 'Ophthalmic Consultants New Jersey' appeared in search results; I could not load that page to verify whether there is any affiliation, so no relationship is asserted.

No phone calls were made and no forms were submitted anywhere, per the read-only limits. Hours, insurance acceptance and pricing therefore rest on what each site publishes; none of the practices publishes price ranges, so price-range answerability could not be assessed beyond 'absent'.
